greetings: Welcome, traveler, to the heart of the savanna! The spirits brought you here, or maybe you just got lost.
Ah, a visitor! Come, sit by the fire and hear the tales of our people, after you pay the entrance fee.
The ancestors foresaw your arrival. They said you'd be taller.
guild_master.reward: The tribe honors your deeds! Take this artifact, blessed by the rain gods and my grandmother.

farmer: The ancestors whispered to me last night... they said 'plant more carrots'.
My acacia hoe is unbreakable, much like my spirit when a creeper blew up my crops.
I offer these beetroots to the spirits of the rain. Please, we need precipitation, not more zombie groans.
Some say I talk to my wheat. I say, my wheat gives better advice than the Nitwit.
If a lion eats my sheep, I am sad. If a ravager eats my crops, I am going to war.
The sun is hot, but my compost bin is hotter. Literally, it's smoking. Help.
You cannot hurry the harvest, but you can certainly hurry away from a spider.
A wise elder once told me: never trust a man who prefers poisonous potatoes.
This melon? Grown on the sacred grounds of my forefathers. Ten emeralds.
I am the master of the savanna soil. Tremble before my... pumpkins.
fisherman: The watering hole is full of crocodiles, hippos, and exactly three cod.
I fished up a leather boot. I believe it belonged to my great-grandfather.
The spirits of the river demand a sacrifice. I offered them a stick.
A true fisherman does not need a rod, only patience. And maybe a rod. Actually, yes, sell me a rod.
I stare at the water until it gives me fish. It is a battle of wills.
I once caught a fish so big, it swallowed a baby zombie. True story.
The crocodiles respect me. The salmon, however, are deeply insolent.
Fishing under the acacia tree is peaceful, until the pillagers start shooting.
May your nets be full and your boat un-exploded.
This tropical fish holds the wisdom of a thousand generations. Don't eat it.
shepherd: My sheep are not just wool providers; they are my tribe.
I sheared a sheep, and beneath the wool... was another, angrier sheep.
The lions look at my flock with hunger. I look at the lions with a pair of shears.
An elder told me counting sheep helps you sleep. It only helps me calculate my profits.
Wool of orange, wool of brown, matching the savanna sun going down.
Keep your voice low. The sheep are discussing the philosophy of grass.
I trade wool for emeralds. I trade emeralds for more sheep. It's the circle of life.
Have you ever tried to dye a sheep while it's running? It requires ancestral guidance.
The ancestors watch over my flock. Except when it rains, then they go inside.
A sheared sheep is a cold sheep, but a wealthy shepherd is a happy shepherd.
fletcher: My arrows fly straighter than a gazelle running from a cheetah.
I craft these bows from the finest acacia. They snap sometimes, but it builds character.
An arrow to the knee? Please, my ancestors took arrows to the face and kept farming.
Feathers from the sacred ostriches... wait, no, just regular chickens. Don't tell anyone.
I put flint on a stick and charge you emeralds. I am an economic genius.
The spirits guide my aim. That's my excuse when I miss the target completely.
Buy my arrows, or I will use them for target practice. You are the target.
A bow without arrows is just a very inconvenient curved stick.
May your aim be true and your string never snap in front of a skeleton.
I once shot an arrow so far, it hit the sun. That's why it gets dark at night.
cleric: The spirits of the savanna demand flesh! Rotten flesh, specifically. Two emeralds for ten.
I brew potions using the tears of my enemies and some nether wart.
The ancestors speak to me. Mostly they complain about my posture.
I can heal your wounds, but I cannot heal your terrible fashion sense.
Do not anger the spirits, or they will spawn a creeper in your house.
This glowstone dust contains the trapped souls of fireflies. Or so I tell the children.
I have stared into the void, and the void offered me a discount on ender pearls.
My lapis lazuli is blessed by the rain gods. It also stains everything blue.
Cleanse your spirit! And your inventory. Give me your gold.
A zombie villager is just a relative who hasn't had their morning coffee.
weaponsmith: I forge swords sharp enough to slice the heat in half.
An iron sword is good, but a diamond sword shows you have financial responsibility.
The elders say violence is not the answer. They clearly never met a Ravager.
I heat my forge with the burning rage of a thousand suns. And some coal.
A dull blade is an insult to your ancestors. Buy a sharp one.
I once fought a lion with my bare hands. Then I learned to make swords.
My axes do not chop wood, they chop bad vibes.
May your blade never chip, and your enemies always drop good loot.
I sell weapons of mass destruction. Please use responsibly on zombies.
The spirits guide my hammer. Sometimes they guide it directly onto my thumb.
armorer: My armor can withstand a rhino charge. I haven't tested it, but trust me.
Wearing iron in the savanna heat? You are either very brave or very foolish.
Diamond armor sparkles like the stars over the Serengeti.
I pounded this chestplate until my arms fell off. The spirits reattached them.
Protection from arrows, zombies, and the harsh judgment of your mother-in-law.
A shield is just a door you carry with you. Buy my portable doors!
The ancestors wore nothing but leather. The ancestors also died early. Buy iron.
If a creeper explodes and you're wearing my armor, you will be a very well-preserved corpse.
May your boots never wear out, and your helmet never fall off.
I make helmets that fit perfectly over your massive, blocky head.
toolsmith: My pickaxes break rock, dirt, and occasionally, the laws of physics.
A good shovel is the difference between a house and a dirt hut.
I craft hoes of such quality, the dirt practically tills itself out of respect.
An iron axe? Good. A diamond axe? Now you're chopping with ancestral power.
The spirits told me to make tools. They didn't say who would buy them, but here you are.
My tools are guaranteed to last a lifetime. Unless you fall in lava.
A blunt pickaxe is a sign of a weak spirit. And a weak bank account.
I can fix your tools, but I can't fix your terrible mining habits.
May your tunnels be straight and your diamonds plentiful.
This flint and steel will burn your enemies, or your own house. Choose wisely.
butcher: I respect the animals of the savanna. Then I turn them into porkchops.
The ancestors hunted with spears. I hunt with a very sharp cleaver and a corral.
Nothing beats a good steak cooked over an open acacia fire.
I have beef with everyone. Literally, I sell beef.
A moment of silence for the chickens. Okay, moment over, who wants nuggets?
My sausages are a secret tribal recipe. Mostly pig, maybe some mystery meat.
The spirits demand a feast! And I demand payment in emeralds.
I chop the meat with the fury of a thousand rhinos.
May your belly be full and your food poisoning nonexistent.
I once butchered a hoglin. The meat tasted like burning and regret.
leatherworker: The hide of a cow, the spirit of a warrior, the fashion sense of a confused trader.
I tan this leather under the brutal savanna sun. It builds character. And smell.
Leather pants in this heat? You are making a bold choice, my friend.
I can make a saddle fit for a horse, a pig, or a particularly large child.
The ancestors wore leather. I dye it pink so they can't recognize me.
My horse armor will make your steed look magnificent, right before it walks into a ravine.
Dyeing leather is an art passed down through generations. Mostly involving squids.
May your boots never squeak when you are sneaking past a warden.
I sell the finest leather tunics. Perfect for sweating profusely.
I make leather items. Please stop asking if I have vegan options.
mason: I take rocks and make them into slightly different shaped rocks.
Terracotta is the lifeblood of savanna architecture. And it looks pretty.
I stare at stone all day. Sometimes the stone stares back.
The spirits reside in the stones. I cut them into neat little bricks anyway.
Building a dirt hut? The ancestors weep for you. Buy my bricks.
I chisel with the patience of a lion stalking a gazelle.
Quartz? In this economy? You must be royalty.
May your walls be straight and your creepers far away.
I once built a statue of myself out of diorite. The village burned it down.
My stone blocks are guaranteed to be heavy and hard. Just like life.
cartographer: I map the savanna, from the tallest acacia to the deepest, most terrifying ravine.
The ancestors navigated by the stars. I navigate by charging you for paper.
I have a map to a woodland mansion. It mostly involves walking for three weeks.
The world is flat, my maps prove it. Don't argue with science.
I got lost in my own village yesterday, but my maps are flawless, I swear.
An unmapped world is an insult to my profession. Go explore it for me.
I draw little monsters on the edges of the map where I haven't been.
May your paths be clear and your compass never spin wildly.
I trade glass panes for emeralds. I don't know why, it just works.
I have mapped the stars, the rivers, and exactly where the iron golem is stuck.
librarian: The oral traditions of my people are sacred. But I write them down anyway. Better for business.
A book of Mending will fix your tools, but not your broken heart.
I have read every book in this village. All three of them.
The elders say knowledge is power. I say knowledge is worth twenty emeralds.
Silence in the library! The spirits are trying to read.
I have a book on how to survive a zombie attack. It just says 'RUN' on every page.
Enchanted books contain the whispers of the ancestors. And some really confusing grammar.
May your bookshelves be full and your reading glasses strong.
I trade paper for emeralds. It's a scam, but don't tell the others.
I once read a book so profound, my brain leveled up.
nitwit: The ancestors tell me to do nothing. I am very obedient.
I am observing the grass. It is a very complex process.
Work is for people who don't appreciate the beauty of a nap.
I am the spiritual anchor of this village. By sitting here and doing nothing.
The spirits spoke to me. They said, 'Go back to sleep'.
I'm not lazy, I'm just operating on a higher plane of energy conservation.
Some chop wood, some farm. I... I breathe. It's important.
My shirt is green, like the grass I sleep on.
If you run fast enough, the work can't catch you.
I am currently busy contemplating a single grain of sand. Please come back later.
none: I am searching for my calling. Hopefully, it pays well.
The spirits have not yet assigned me a profession. I am a free agent.
I stand here, waiting for a block to be placed. Any block.
I am a blank canvas, ready to be painted by the brush of capitalism.
Give me a composter and I will show you the meaning of life.
I have no job, no emeralds, but I have a lot of free time.
The elders say I have potential. I think they mean I take up space.
I am currently unemployed, but I am accepting donations.
My dream is to be a Nitwit, but it requires too much dedication.
I wander the village, offering unsolicited advice and getting in the way.

generic: Hrm. The sun is hot today.
Hah? Have you seen the iron golem? He owes me money.
Hmm. The acacia trees whisper your name. Mostly complaining.
Hrm. Welcome to the savanna, mind the heat.
Hahh. We honor the spirits by trading fairly. And overcharging tourists.
Hrmm. The rains will come when the rains will come.
Hmm. If you see a pillager, please point them towards the Nitwit.
Hah. May the spirits guide your steps away from my crops.
Hrm. Life is like a block of dirt. You can build with it, or you can fall on it.

greetings: I am practicing my stealth crouch! Did I startle you, or are you just naturally jumpy?
Elder Kael said if I catch a cheetah, I get to name it. I'm gonna name it Speedy Fluff!
Check out my spear! It's just a sharp stick, but I painted cool red stripes on it.
I tried tracking an elephant today, but it turned out to be a really big rock.
If you see a lion, just act like a tree. Lions hate trees. Probably.
I'm practicing my war cry! AAAAAAAH—wait, my throat hurts now.
The elders say I have the spirit of an eagle, but my mom says I have the appetite of a warthog.
Look at this beetle! It rolls dirt balls! I'm trying to teach it to roll emeralds instead.
I bet I can outrun an ostrich! ...Okay, maybe a very tired ostrich.
My big brother told me acacia leaves taste like sweet candy. He lied. My tongue is numb.
Are you a warrior from afar? Can you show me how to throw a boomerang without hitting myself?
I made a camouflage suit out of tall grass! Now nobody can see me... wait, why are you staring at me?
I found a vulture feather! If I plant it in the dirt, will a vulture tree grow?
I'm on a secret hunting mission. Target: the village cat. Status: it scratched my nose.
When I grow up, I'm going to lead the great savanna hunt! But right now, I have nap time.
I hid behind an acacia tree, but my shadow was so long it gave me away!
Do you think hyenas tell jokes? They're always laughing at something.
I challenged a zebra to a race. It ignored me, which technically means I won by forfeit!
My dad taught me how to read animal tracks. These ones mean 'a pig walked here, and then it got confused'.
I made a mud mask like the hunters use. Now it dried and I can't smile!
I tried to tame a baby gazelle, but it jumped over my head and ran into the bush.
The sun is super bright today! My shadow is so short, I think it melted.
I painted my face like a fierce lion, but my mom said I look like a muddy papaya.
I'm building the world's biggest dirt mound! Don't step on it, it's a sacred monument.
Uncle says vultures fly in circles when something is dying. They've been following my cooking all morning.
My brother played hide-and-seek with a leopard last week. We're still looking for him!
I found a shiny skeleton near the waterhole! I named him Skelly and he's my best friend now.
Elder Omu says the spirits take those who walk alone at night... so I send my little brother out first!
A crocodile stole my wooden shield yesterday. Luckily, it took my thumb drive too—wait, what's a thumb drive?
If a lion eats me, at least I won't have to clean the mud hut tonight!

cookie_success: Mmm! This sweet disk is way better than dried termite paste! Thank you, traveler!
A crunchy brown treat! I will offer a crumb to the ancestors, but the rest goes straight into my tummy!
Whoa, so delicious! If I feed this to a wild boar, will it become friendly, or just fat?
cookie_fail_1: Aw, no sweet disk for me? I guess I'll go back to chewing on acacia bark...
You're keeping the treat for yourself? My tummy is playing the sacred drum of hunger!
No cookie? Fine, I'll ask the village elder. He gives me dried berries if I pretend to listen to his stories!
cookie_fail_2: Still nothing? Even the vultures are judging your lack of generosity!
Are you really going to eat that in front of a growing warrior? The spirits are watching, traveler!
Denied twice?! I'm going to tell the hunting chief that you hoarded all the rations!
sugar_rush: WOAH! SPEED OF THE CHEETAH! STRENGTH OF THE ELEPHANT! I CAN RUN ACROSS THE WHOLE SAVANNA!
MY FEET ARE ON FIRE! I'M GONNA CHASE A ZEBRA! NO, THREE ZEBRAS AT ONCE! WATCH ME GOOO!
TOO MUCH ENERGY! I JUST LEAPED OVER A BAOBAB BUSH AND CAUGHT A FLY WITH MY TEETH!
sugar_fail: Ugh... my head is spinning faster than a tribal dancer... I need to sit under an acacia tree...
Oof, the sugar spirit has abandoned me! My legs feel like heavy mud bricks...
Urgh... tummy hurt... I think I'm gonna turn into vulture bait if I don't nap right now...
toy_success: A toy! I shall train with this every day until I am the greatest hunter in the valley!
Awesome! This is way cooler than playing with sun-dried rhino dung!
Thank you! I will name this toy 'Lion-Slayer' and take it on all my secret backyard quests!
toy_fail: No toy? That's okay, I still have my favorite pointy stick and a very round stone.
Aw man... I guess I'll just go back to wrestling small bushes for fun.
You're keeping it? Fine, but if a hyena sneaks into your tent tonight, don't blame me!
parents: My dad is the chief tracker! He can smell a warthog from three miles away... especially after lunch!
My mom makes us wear mud paint every morning. She says it keeps bugs away, but I think she just likes how silly we look.
My uncle tried to wrestle an ostrich once. Now he walks with a permanent wiggle and talks to clouds.
rps_win: HA! Rock smashes your scissors! Just like a hunter crushing a stubborn nut!
YES! Paper covers rock! My leaf snare trap caught your heavy boulder!
I WIN! My wooden shears cut right through your woven grass rope! VICTORY WAR CRY!
rps_lose: Ah, defeated! You wielded your hand sign with the quickness of a striking cobra!
Outsmarted by a traveler! I must return to the elder and study the ancient art of hand gestures.
Nooo! My rock got wrapped in paper! How is paper even strong enough to do that?!
rps_tie: A draw! We are matched like two young lions locking horns in the tall grass!
Same sign! The ancestors have decreed that our minds are walking the exact same trail!
Another tie! Quick, throw again before the sun sets and the hyenas take over the game!
